nodes.name: Ni foam pretreatment
nodes.procedure: A piece of Ni foam (2 cm×3 cm) was ultrasonically cleaned in a 6 M HCl solution for 15 min to remove the surface oxide layer. This was followed by sequential washing with deionized water, anhydrous ethanol, and acetone, and the foam was subsequently dried under argon flow for further use.

nodes.name: Ru SAs@NiFeV-LTHs hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 1.67 mmol of FeCl₃, 0.5 mmol of VCl₃, 0.02 mmol of RuCl₃, and 4 mmol of urea were dispersed in 20 mL of deionized water. The resulting solution mixture was stirred for 2 h to achieve a homogeneous solution. The cleaned Ni foam was immersed in this solution and then transferred into a 25 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave. The autoclave was heated to 120°C for 6 h in an electric oven, followed by cooling to room temperature. The resulting product was washed with deionized water, anhydrous ethanol, and acetone, and finally dried under argon flow to obtain Ru SAs@NiFeV-LTHs.

nodes.name: NiFeV-LTHs hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: A similar procedure was used for the synthesis of NiFeV-LTHs on Ni foam, but without the introduction of RuCl₃. [Includes: Ni foam pretreatment, 1.67 mmol FeCl₃, 0.5 mmol VCl₃, 4 mmol urea in 20 mL water, stirring 2 h, hydrothermal at 120°C for 6 h, washing, drying under Ar flow.]

nodes.characterization_summary: Nanosheets showed lattice fringes with d-spacing of 2.58 Å corresponding to (012) planes of NiFe-based hydroxides.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Structural analysis of these nanosheets revealed lattice fringes with a d-spacing of 2.58 Å, corresponding to the (012) planes of NiFe-based hydroxides (Figure 1d,e,h,i).

nodes.characterization_summary: Atomic dispersion of Ru single atoms confirmed on NiFeV-LTHs support with higher Z contrast; no Ru clusters or nanoparticles detected.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) imaging further confirmed the atomic dispersion of Ru over the NiFeV-LTHs support... Owing to their higher atomic number Z, Ru SAs exhibited a heavier image contrast.

nodes.characterization_summary: V 2p and Ru 3p signals confirmed incorporation; Ni/Fe binding energies shifted due to V and Ru doping; Ru 3p doublets at 462.4 eV (3p3/2) and 485.0 eV (3p1/2) indicate Ru3+.
nodes.evidence_snippet: XPS survey spectra clearly showed the presence of V 2p signals for NiFeV-LTHs and V 2p/Ru 3p signals for Ru SAs@NiFeVLTHs... the binding energies of Ni and Fe in NiFeV-LTHs and Ru SAs@NiFeV-LTHs exhibited shifts... Ru 3p spectrum displayed two doublets (Ru 3p3/2 and Ru 3p1/2) at 462.4 and 485.0 eV, which closely resembled the standard RuCl3 and is therefore characteristic of Ru3+.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru SAs@NiFeV-LTHs showed ECSA of 64.75 cm⁻² (vs 32.50 cm⁻² for NiFe-LDHs, 41.75 cm⁻² for NiFeV-LTHs) calculated from Cdl.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ru SAs@NiFeV-LTHs exhibited a greater ECSA value (64.75 cm⁻²) than NiFe-LDHs (32.50 cm⁻²) and NiFeV-LTHs (41.75 cm⁻²) indicating a greater number of electrochemically active sites.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES shows oxidation state between 0 and 4+; FT-EXAFS peaks at 1.98 Å (Ru-O, CN=4.5) and 2.69 Å (Ru-O-M, CN=0.26); WT confirms Ru-O coordination, absence of Ru-Ru scattering.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Analysis of the Ru adsorption edge revealed an oxidation state between 0 and 4+ (Figure 5a)... FT-EXAFS spectrum displayed distinct peaks at 1.98 and 2.69 Å... coordination numbers of 4.5 for Ru-O and 0.26 for Ru-O-M... WT intensity maximum at k≈6.4 Å⁻¹ attributed to Ru-O coordination... No WT intensity maximum at k≈10.3 Å⁻¹, suggesting absence of metallic Ru clusters.
